title: Synthetic universes: map, mechanism and the law-extractor trap
summary: MatrixInMatrix and phi-world-theory use the same broad Buckyball / best.py synthetic-universe material for a useful epistemic question: what has actually been learned when a complicated world can be predicted or reconstructed compactly? MatrixInMatrix gives the cleanest version by contrasting the original nonlinear field with a harmonic reconstruction that can reproduce the stable shape while losing the source dynamics that heal and evolve it. phi-world-theory expands that workflow into predictors, harmonic probes, dimensional analyses and a master-vector story, but its own README explicitly warns that parts are AI slop, hallucinated concepts and short logical jumps. The atlas therefore keeps the workflow and the map-versus-territory question while refusing to treat predictive accuracy, compression or suggestive algebra as identification of the source physics.

nodes.claim: Builds a three-layer synthetic-world experiment: a nonlinear field produces a stable Buckyball, an observer extracts a compact harmonic fingerprint with a 3-D FFT, and a separate renderer reconstructs the shape from that compressed description.
nodes.survived: The useful result is the compression-versus-mechanism distinction. The repo's reconstructed harmonic map can reproduce the recognizable Buckyball while deliberately abandoning the original field dynamics; the original object can heal and evolve after perturbation, whereas the clean reconstruction is a static descriptive copy.
nodes.killed: A compact or visually convincing reconstruction does not establish that the extracted harmonics are the source mechanism that generated the original field dynamics. The map can be an excellent compression while still omitting the causal machinery responsible for evolution, repair and response to perturbation.

nodes.claim: Collects a larger synthetic-universe workflow around best.py: next-state prediction, harmonic extraction, perturbation tests, symmetry/dimensional probes and a high-dimensional-vector interpretation are used to ask how an observer might infer compact laws from an artificial world.
nodes.survived: The reusable workflow is simulate -> predict/extract -> perturb -> analyze -> compare interpretations. The README explicitly credits the older SpaceScreensaver scenario, whose implementation is archived here. Another durable origin is state -> lens -> appearance: a hidden vector can admit several observationally identical sources, making the reader and its interventions part of the question. The October code/algebra revisit measures a rank-12 master lens with 988 invisible complex directions and connects this observability problem to MoonFormer's actual consequence probes. The synthetic generator remains available for checking proposed laws.
nodes.killed: The README itself warns that there is AI slop, hallucinated material and logical jumps. Prediction or supplied harmonic reconstruction does not identify the source physics. The 131.47% figure is a sum over overlapping readout directions, not a captured-energy fraction or proof of holography: the specified frame permits 139.96% raw response for a unit state, while correct orthogonal projection is bounded by 100%. The fixed twelve-row lens cannot identify a unique 1000D source. Direct algebra controls also find an almost-identical supposed alien memory, phase steering erased by magnitude readout, and rank-two three-phase mixing. The origin of the ideas survives; cosmology, general recall and unique physics do not follow from these demos.

motifs.title: A model of a world is not necessarily the mechanism that made the world
motifs.description: MatrixInMatrix makes the boundary visual: a compressed harmonic reconstruction can reproduce the observed object while dropping the field dynamics that heal and evolve it. phi-world-theory asks the same question with prediction and deeper mathematical probes. Good prediction, compact reconstruction and suggestive latent structure are evidence that observations admit a useful model; they do not by themselves identify the source mechanism that generated the world.
